claims.explanation: Zardaverine is a dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor that raises cAMP; selectivity likely reflects dependence on cAMP-hydrolyzing PDE activity, particularly PDE4D, and on intact cAMP-PKA signaling. Lines with high PDE4D expression or cAMP-dependent survival (e.g., BRAF-mutant melanoma, KRAS-mutant pancreatic/colorectal, EGFR-mutant lung) are sensitized, whereas lines with PTEN loss, high PI3K/AKT signaling, or low PDE4D are protected. The pattern is consistent with cAMP-mediated growth inhibition and apoptosis rather than a single lineage.

features.basis: direct drug target; high expression increases cAMP hydrolysis dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among sensitive lines; cAMP/PKA cross-talk with MAPK
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, counteracting cAMP-mediated apoptosis; enriched in resistant lines
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear among sensitive lines; cAMP signaling intersects with EGFR/MAPK
TP53 mutation is common in both groups but may blunt cAMP-induced apoptosis
CDKN2A loss may increase dependence on cAMP-mediated cell-cycle arrest
NF1 loss elevates RAS/MAPK, potentially increasing cAMP cross-talk sensitivity
PIK3CA mutation activates PI3K/AKT, reducing cAMP-mediated killing
ATM loss may impair DNA-damage response and reduce apoptosis from cAMP elevation
ARID1A loss may alter chromatin and increase cAMP-responsive gene expression
SMARCA4 loss may reduce transcriptional response to cAMP
